Ibn Umar divorced his wife during her menses; the Prophet, angry, ordered him to take her back and divorce, if he wished, only when she is clean and untouched.
The Prophet had Ibn Umar, who divorced his wife during menses, take her back until a later purity, then keep or divorce her; that divorce was counted as one.
When Al-Jaun's daughter, brought to the Prophet as a bride, sought refuge with Allah from him, he told her to return to her family, giving her two linen dresses.
A menses divorce counted; Uwaimir divorced thrice after li'an; a thrice-divorced wife returns only after another husband consummates marriage; the option the Prophet gave his wives was no divorce.
Allah forgives the Prophet's followers evil thoughts not acted upon or spoken, and Qatada said a divorce made only in the mind has no effect.
Thabit bin Qais's wife, finding no fault in his character or religion yet unable to stay with him, returned his garden, and the Prophet had him divorce her.
Freed and given the choice, Barira left her slave husband Mughith despite his tears and the Prophet's intercession; wala goes to whoever frees, and alms given her became a gift.
The Prophet ended his oath of abstention from his wives after twenty-nine days; Ibn Umar said after Ila's four months a husband must keep his wife well or divorce her.
Rifa'a's divorced wife, remarried to an impotent man, was told she could not return to Rifa'a until the second husband consummated the marriage.
Aisha faulted a divorced woman for leaving her husband's house, and rebuked Fatima bint Qais for saying such women get no housing or upkeep, since Fatima left an unsafe place.
Ma'qil, refusing to let his divorced sister remarry her former husband, yielded when verse 2:232 came down; Ibn Umar, who divorced in menses, was ordered to take his wife back.
Rifa'a's irrevocably divorced wife, describing her new husband by her veil's fringe, is told she cannot return to Rifa'a until Abdur-Rahman consummates their marriage.
Rifa'a's divorced wife, her skin bruised green, calls Abdur-Rahman impotent; he denies it, and the Prophet says she cannot return to Rifa'a without consummation, noting the sons resembling him.
Angry that Ibn Umar divorced his wife in her menses, the Prophet ordered him to take her back and keep her through another period before divorcing, if he wished.
